hidden_note: 28 trophies are hidden on PlayStation until earned. The kit's starter did not carry per-trophy hidden flags, so hidden flags here mark the story and secret trophies (the chapter and mission trophies, the stranger-strand finals and the secret event trophies), totalling 28 to match the published count. The exact hidden set should be re-checked against PSNProfiles once the game is out.
list: The official 55 trophies, as published by PlayStation and listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles (2026-11-18). Names, descriptions and grades are the official ones. Guides are this entry's own words, written from the official descriptions; where a place or step cannot be verified from the description alone, the guide says so plainly instead of inventing it.
sources_note: Sources are named, never copied. 'ref' values are domain paths without a scheme, so the app makes no network request: a reader can type the path into a browser. The official list: Exophase, exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/ — PSNProfiles, psnprofiles.com/trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi

trophies.guide: The platinum pops by itself the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing to do for it directly. Work through this guide's roadmap: finish the story, the stranger strands, the collectibles and the activities, then clean up the 100% requirements. When the last of the 54 lands, this one follows immediately.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies — story, side strands, collectibles and activities.
Watch the progress bar at the top of this guide; 54 of 55 means one trophy is left.
The platinum unlocks automatically once the last one pops; no extra step is needed.

trophies.guide: 'Gone Fishing' is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players earn: just play through the intro until the mission ends. It cannot be missed — the story takes you through it — and it unlocks the moment the mission completes.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
steps: Start a new game and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing.
Follow the on-screen objectives until the mission ends.

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 1 to its end. A chapter trophy unlocks automatically when the last mission of the chapter finishes, so there is nothing special to do — keep playing the story in order and this pops at the chapter break.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
steps: Play the story missions of Chapter 1 in order.
The trophy pops when the chapter's final mission completes.

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 2 to its end. Like every chapter trophy, it unlocks automatically when the chapter's final mission completes — keep playing the story in order and it pops at the chapter break.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
steps: Play the story missions of Chapter 2 in order.
The trophy pops when the chapter's final mission completes.

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 3 to its end. It unlocks automatically when the chapter's final mission completes — keep playing the story in order and it pops at the chapter break.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
steps: Play the story missions of Chapter 3 in order.
The trophy pops when the chapter's final mission completes.

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 4 to its end. It unlocks automatically when the chapter's final mission completes — keep playing the story in order and it pops at the chapter break.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
steps: Play the story missions of Chapter 4 in order.
The trophy pops when the chapter's final mission completes.

trophies.confirm: Whether stranger strands stay available after the finale is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. It unlocks when the story ends, after the last mission's objectives complete. Before you start the finale, finish the stranger strands and the choice-based trophy 'Actions Speak Louder' — the official description does not say whether those stay available afterwards, so do them first to be safe.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Complete Chapters 1 to 4 and every mission leading to the finale.
Before the final mission, finish all stranger strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) and the choices for 'Actions Speak Louder'.
Play the final mission to its end; the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission 'Breakfast Run'. Story missions unlock in order as you play; this one pops the moment the mission's objectives are done. It only needs a completion, not a rating or a special approach.
trophies.name: Trust
steps: Play the story until the mission Breakfast Run unlocks.
Finish the mission; the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission 'The Cartel Heist'. It pops the moment the heist's objectives are done. It only needs a completion, not a rating or a special approach.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
steps: Play the story until the mission The Cartel Heist unlocks.
Finish the mission; the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.name: Family Matters

Finish the mission; the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.name: DWNFALL

Finish the mission; the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.confirm: The exact 100% requirements are not in the official description; they must be read from the in-game checklist.
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion. The in-game stats screen tracks what counts toward 100% — story missions, stranger strands, collectibles and activities among them. Work through this guide's roadmap and the 100% checklist in the pause menu. The official description does not spell out the exact requirements, so read each category from the in-game checklist rather than assuming a trophy is the last one left.
trophies.name: A Long Road

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Open the in-game 100% checklist (pause menu / stats) and note every category it lists.
Finish the story, all stranger strands, collectibles and activities in this guide.
Re-check the list after each session — the last unchecked item is what stands between you and this trophy.

trophies.confirm: Which actions count as a 'stunt' is not defined in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts, counted cumulatively across the whole game. Stunts are the driving tricks the game tracks — jumps, airtime, near misses and similar feats — and they add up as you play, so a large share will come naturally from the story and from driving hard around Leonida. To grind the rest, chain jumps and near misses on open roads and check the in-game stats to see the counter move. The official description does not define exactly which actions count as a stunt, so confirm the counter in-game before grinding one trick for hours.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Play the story and drive aggressively — stunts accumulate as you go.
Check the in-game stats for the stunt counter to see your progress.
Grind the remainder with jumps and near misses on open roads.

trophies.confirm: The 9 activity types are not named in the official description; they must be read from the in-game activities menu.
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try one of each of the 9 activity types the game counts. Open the activities menu in-game and work down its list — races, the shooting range, fishing, the arcade, bowling, drone races, meditation, hunting and the rest — doing one of each. The official description does not name the 9 types, so use the in-game list to see which ones you have tried and which remain.
trophies.name: Master of None

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Open the in-game activities menu and note its 9 types.
Do one activity of each type — a race, a shooting range challenge, a fishing trip, and so on.
Check the menu again; any type left untried is still to do.

trophies.confirm: Gold-medal score thresholds per challenge are not in the official description; they are shown in-game per challenge.
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Each challenge shows its gold score or time in-game before you start it, so the target is always visible — the work is hitting it. Take your time, learn each challenge's layout, and use the range's practice runs before going for gold. Progress is per challenge, so you can gold them in any order and come back to the hard ones last.
trophies.name: The Shootist
steps: Visit a shooting range and open its challenge list.
Read each challenge's gold target before starting it.
Gold the easy challenges first, then practise the hard ones until the gold score lands.

trophies.confirm: The 14 race locations are not named in the official description; they are shown on the in-game map once Top Fun races are found.
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. A location counts once you have won a race there, so you need 14 wins in 14 different places — winning the same location twice does not help. Find the Top Fun race spots on the map, win one race at each, and keep a note of which locations are done. The official description does not name the 14 spots, so find them through the in-game map and race markers.
trophies.name: Top Fun
steps: Find Top Fun drone race locations on the in-game map.
Win one race at a location to tick it off.
Work through all 14 locations, keeping track of the ones already won.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Each distinct race counts once, so you need 20 wins across 20 different races — re-winning the same race does not add to the count. Mix race types (road, off-road, drone, boat or whatever the game offers) and work through the race list; races you have already won are the ones to skip. This overlaps with the Top Fun races, so the 14 drone-race wins count toward it too.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
steps: Open the race list and note which races you have already won.
Win races you have not won before, across different race types.
Keep going until 20 different races are won.

trophies.confirm: When Cal's fishing challenge unlocks is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the fishing contact you meet through the game's fishing — take the challenge he offers and out-fish him on whatever the challenge scores (catch count, weight or a target fish). If the challenge is not offered yet, keep fishing and progressing the story until Cal's challenge appears; the official description does not say when it unlocks.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Go fishing and meet Cal through the game's fishing activities.
Accept Cal's fishing challenge when he offers it.
Out-score him on the challenge's target and the trophy pops.

trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game to its end. Find an arcade cabinet in-game, start a game and play it through to completion — a high score alone is not enough, the game has to be completed. Any arcade game counts, so pick the shortest or easiest one you find.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
steps: Find an arcade machine in the game world.
Start an arcade game and play it to its end.
The trophy pops when the game completes.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's stranger strand. Stranger strands are chains of side missions for people you meet around Leonida — follow Andy's missions through to the last one. This is flagged as possibly missable: the official description does not say whether stranger strands stay open after the final story mission, so finish Andy's strand before the finale to be safe.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

Finish the strand's final mission; the trophy pops on completion.
Do it before the final story mission, in case strands close after the finale.

trophies.confirm: Which 8 strands count is not named in the official description; the in-game stranger menu shows the strands you have found.
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers are the side characters marked around the state — each one has a chain of missions, and a strand counts when its final mission is done. This is the umbrella trophy for the individual strand finals (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and the rest), so it pops once any 8 strands are finished. Flagged as possibly missable alongside the strands themselves: finish them before the finale, in case strands close after it.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.confirm: The 18 meditation spots are not named in the official description; they are found by exploring Leonida and shown on the map once discovered.
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet places in the world — viewpoints, beaches, parks and the like — where the game offers a meditate prompt. Visit each one and meditate there; a spot counts once you have done it. Explore the state thoroughly and check the map for markers you have not visited yet.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
steps: Explore Leonida and look for meditation prompts at scenic spots.
Meditate at each spot you find; it counts once done.
Keep going until all 18 spots are meditated at — check the map for places not yet visited.

trophies.confirm: Which animal is unique for Bret, and where it is found, is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Bret is the hunting contact — take his hunting work, track the animal he names and bring it down. The official description does not name the animal or where it lives, so follow Bret's instructions in-game when the hunt opens up; do not trust a location from an unverified source. The trophy pops when the unique animal is hunted for him.
trophies.name: Fair Game

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Find Bret's hunting work and take the hunt for the unique animal.
Track the animal using the in-game hunting prompts.
Take it down; the trophy pops when the hunt is complete.

trophies.confirm: Which cards belong to which set is not in the official description; sets are shown in the in-game collection menu.
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full sets of collectible cards. Cards are hidden around Leonida — in shops, interiors and out in the world — and they belong to sets shown in the in-game collection menu. Pick up cards as you explore and check the menu to see which sets are close to complete; a set counts when every card in it is found. You need any 3 sets, so focus on the sets with the fewest cards missing.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
steps: Pick up collectible cards as you explore Leonida.
Check the collection menu to see which sets are nearest complete.
Finish any 3 sets; the trophy pops when the third set completes.

trophies.confirm: What 'WAiNK It' is and where its 100 locations are is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.guide: Use the 'WAiNK It' action at 100 different locations. WAiNK It is an in-world action tied to places around Leonida — each location counts once, so you need 100 distinct spots. Work through the map methodically, area by area, and use the in-game counter to see how many locations are done. The official description does not explain what WAiNK It is or where the spots are, so learn the action from the game's own prompts and do not trust an unverified location list.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Learn the WAiNK It action from the game's own prompts.
Use it at a new location to count it; each location counts once.
Work through Leonida area by area until 100 locations are done.

trophies.confirm: The 50 challenges are not listed in the official description; they are shown in the in-game challenges menu.
trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's challenges. Challenges are the small goals listed in the in-game challenges menu — driving feats, combat feats, exploration and more — and they complete naturally as you play the story, the activities and the collectibles. Open the menu to see which challenges are close to done, finish the easy ones first, and let the rest accumulate; 50 is a count across all challenge types, not one category.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
steps: Open the in-game challenges menu and see what is listed.
Complete the challenges closest to done first.
Keep playing story, activities and collectibles — challenges complete as you go — until 50 are done.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. The partner must be with you when the wanted level is lost — do it during a mission or free-roam session where your partner is present, get the cops to 4 stars, then break line of sight, hide until the stars clear, and stay out of sight until the heat is gone. The trophy pops when the wanted level is fully lost.
trophies.name: Hot Together
steps: Make sure your partner is with you.
Commit crimes until the wanted level reaches 4 stars.
Break line of sight and hide until all 4 stars clear.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without the wanted level dropping in between. The chain is the point: rob one shop, move straight to the next while the wanted level is still active, and do the third the same way. If the wanted level clears before the third robbery, the chain breaks and you start over. Pick three shops close together, keep moving, and do not stop to fight the cops.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
steps: Make sure your partner is with you and pick three shops close together.
Rob the first shop to gain a wanted level.
Move straight to the second and third shops and rob them before the wanted level clears.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. A vehicle counts the first time you enter or drive it — a new model you have never used before. Drive everything you see: cars, bikes, trucks, boats and aircraft all count toward the total if they are new to you. Variety is what matters, so take a different vehicle whenever you can instead of sticking to one favourite.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
steps: Enter and drive any vehicle you have not used before — it counts as discovered.
Vary what you drive: cars, bikes, trucks, boats and aircraft.
Keep going until 100 different vehicles are discovered.

trophies.confirm: How Combat Focus is triggered and how long it lasts is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-down aiming mode — activate it when five or more enemies are grouped in front of you, then drop all five before the focus ends. Set it up deliberately: draw a group of enemies together in a firefight, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them fast. One enemy short of five means the attempt does not count, so do not waste the focus on a small group.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Get into a firefight with at least 5 enemies grouped together.
Activate Combat Focus.
Take down all 5 enemies before the focus ends.

trophies.confirm: What counts as an 'unscheduled departure' is not defined in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave Vice City International Airport in a way the airport did not schedule — an unscheduled departure. The natural reading is to take an aircraft (or another vehicle) out of VCIA without going through a scheduled flight: get to the airfield, get a plane moving and leave. The official description does not define the exact trigger, so try the plain reading first — take off from VCIA in a plane you control — and if it does not pop, the trigger is something narrower that still needs pinning down in-game.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Go to Vice City International Airport (VCIA).
Get control of a plane on the airfield.
Take off and leave the airport — an unscheduled departure.

trophies.confirm: What exactly triggers this trophy — surviving, destroying or driving a Rhino — is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.guide: This one is about the Rhino tanks. The description is a joke, not an instruction — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — so the trigger is tied to encountering or dealing with Rhino tanks, most likely at a high wanted level when the military rolls them out. Raise a high wanted level until Rhinos appear, then engage with them; the trophy should pop from the encounter. The exact trigger is not stated in the official description, so this guide does not pretend to know whether it is surviving, destroying or driving one — check the trigger in-game.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Raise a high wanted level until Rhino tanks are sent after you.
Engage with the Rhinos — survive the encounter and deal with them.
If it does not pop, the trigger is narrower than the encounter itself; check it in-game.

trophies.confirm: Which jewelry stores qualify and how detection is judged is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store from start to finish without being detected. Stealth is the whole requirement: get in, take the goods and get out without any guard, camera or alarm spotting you. Plan the approach — go in quiet, avoid sightlines, move slowly — and if you are spotted, leave and try again rather than fighting through it, since detection fails the attempt.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Pick a jewelry store and scout it first — guards, cameras, entrances.
Enter quietly, take the goods and leave without being spotted.
If you are detected, leave and retry; a detected run does not count.

trophies.confirm: Where bank vaults are found is not stated in the official description; vault locations are shown in-game once robbery targets are unlocked.
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Each vault is a robbery target: get in, crack or open the vault, take the money and get clear of the police afterwards — the escape is part of the requirement, so a robbery where you are caught does not count. Do the five one at a time, escaping cleanly each time, and the trophy pops after the fifth escape.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
steps: Find a bank vault robbery target in-game.
Rob the vault, then escape the police cleanly.
Repeat for 5 vaults in total; the trophy pops after the fifth escape.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida — intercept one, stop it, take the money from the back, then lose the police that respond. The escape is part of the requirement: get clear of the wanted level after the robbery and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
steps: Find an armored truck on its route around Leonida.
Stop the truck and take the money.
Escape the police that respond; the trophy pops once you are clear.

trophies.confirm: The 52 areas are not named in the official description; they are the named regions of Leonida shown on the in-game map.
trophies.guide: Visit all 52 areas of Leonida. An area counts once you have set foot (or driven) in it — the map shows the named regions, from Vice City to the swamps and the keys. Work through the map region by region, and use the map itself to spot the places you have not been: an area you have never visited stands out as unvisited ground. This pairs naturally with the collectibles, so explore while hunting cards, meditation spots and WAiNK It locations.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
steps: Open the map and note the named regions of Leonida.
Visit each region — drive or walk into it — until the map shows it as visited.
Work region by region until all 52 areas are explored.

trophies.confirm: The 9 gangs and their Illegal Operations are not named in the official description; gang operations are shown in-game once robbery targets are unlocked.
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one Illegal Operation for each of the 9 gangs. Illegal Operations are gang robbery targets around Leonida — each gang has its own. Hit one operation per gang; robbing two operations of the same gang does not count twice. The in-game robbery targets show which gang an operation belongs to, so check that before each hit and keep a list of the gangs already done.
trophies.name: Pest Control
steps: Find Illegal Operation robbery targets and note which gang each belongs to.
Rob one operation for a gang you have not done yet.
Repeat until one operation of each of the 9 gangs is robbed.

trophies.confirm: Which bar or spot on Ocean Beach counts is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail somewhere on Ocean Beach with a view — a beach bar or a spot overlooking the water. Go to Ocean Beach, find a place that serves drinks with a view of the sea, and order a cocktail there. The trophy is about the moment, not a mission, so take your time and enjoy the view; it pops once the drink is served at the right spot.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Go to Ocean Beach.
Find a bar or viewpoint overlooking the water.
Order and enjoy a cocktail there.

trophies.confirm: Which showroom counts is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle straight out through the front of a vehicle showroom — through the glass, in classic GTA style. Get a car inside a showroom (or take the showroom's own display car), point it at the front windows and floor it. The smash is the point: leave through the glass, not the door, and the trophy pops as you burst out onto the street.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Find a vehicle showroom and get a car inside it.
Point the car at the showroom's front glass.
Drive straight out through the glass.

trophies.confirm: What 'follow-through' means here — a full game, a strike, a specific shot — is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bowl at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley and follow through — play a proper game there rather than just walking in. Go to the alley, start a bowling game and play it through; 'follow-through' is the bowling term for completing your throw, so the trophy is most likely about finishing a game (or a full frame) at this specific alley. The official description does not spell out the exact requirement, so play a full game there and check whether it pops.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
Start a bowling game and play it through.
If it does not pop after one game, the requirement is a specific shot or score — check it in-game.

trophies.confirm: What exactly triggers this trophy is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.guide: This one is deliberately vague: 'A partnership with mass appeal.' The plain reading is a moment with your partner that reaches a wide audience — something the two of you do together that gets noticed, such as a public stunt, a viral-style moment or a shared activity that draws a crowd. The official description gives no activity, place or number, so this guide will not invent one: play the partner content, watch for moments where the partnership is the point, and check the trigger in-game.
trophies.name: Personal Best

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Play the partner content — missions and activities done together.
Watch for moments where the partnership itself is the focus.
The exact trigger is not in the official description; check it in-game.

trophies.confirm: What counts as a 'choice' toward the 500 PSN tracks is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks progress toward this trophy up to 500. Choices are the decisions the game offers you, in story missions, stranger strands and side content, where you pick one path over another. Keep choosing as you play rather than avoiding decisions, and the counter climbs. This is flagged as possibly missable: a choice, once made, cannot be unmade, and some choices may lock off content — so if a decision feels big, it probably is one of the 500, and there may be no way back to the other branch on the same playthrough.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

sources.label: Our own reading of the official description — not yet checked in the game

steps: Play the story and side content, making decisions whenever the game offers a choice.
Do not avoid choice prompts — each one counts toward the 500.
Think before big decisions: a choice cannot be unmade on the same playthrough.

trophies.confirm: Which activity this refers to is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.guide: Fail something, then succeed on the second try — 'Second time's the charm.' The plain reading is that an activity you fail once and then pass on the immediate retry pops this trophy. The official description does not say which activity, so the honest advice is: when you fail an activity or challenge, retry it right away instead of walking off, and the second-try success is likely to trigger it. Which activity counts still needs pinning down in-game.

Retry it immediately.
Succeed on the second attempt — the trophy should pop.

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the game's weird, unexplained event. 'What the hell just happened?' is the reaction the trophy is named for, so the trigger is a random or hidden encounter out in the world: something paranormal, absurd or out of place that you stumble across while exploring. There is no activity to start and no mission to follow; explore Leonida's odd corners and the event will find you. The official description does not say what or where it is, so this guide does not invent a location for it.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by — a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a pedestrian, lean out and strike them with a melee weapon as you pass, bowling them over. It is a drive-by with a melee weapon rather than a gun, so any melee weapon works; the hit has to land while you are in a moving vehicle.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
steps: Get a melee weapon and a vehicle.
Drive slowly past a pedestrian.
Strike them with the melee weapon as you pass — a melee drive-by.

trophies.confirm: Which contacts launder Marked Bills and how the exchange works is not stated in the official description; it still needs checking in the game.
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are the dirty money you pick up from robberies and heists — they cannot be spent as-is, so take them to a contact who launders them into clean cash. The total is cumulative: every dollar laundered counts toward the $250,000, so keep feeding marked bills to your contacts after every big score until the total is reached.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops. The total is cumulative and counts every shop in the game — clothes, weapons, food, vehicle mods and everything else. Just play and buy what you need and the total climbs; if you are close to the target, the fastest way to finish it is to spend on big-ticket items such as vehicles or weapon upgrades. The trophy pops the moment your lifetime shop spending passes $100,000.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
steps: Buy what you need from any shop — clothes, weapons, food, vehicle mods.
Spending counts cumulatively across all shops.
The trophy pops when lifetime shop spending passes $100,000.

trophies.confirm: The 8 garage properties are not named in the official description; they are the garages for sale on the in-game property market.
trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties. Garages are bought through the in-game property market — check it for garages for sale, buy each one, and keep an eye on your money: garages are not cheap, so save up or earn first and buy them as you can afford them. The trophy pops when the eighth garage is yours.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
steps: Open the in-game property market and find garages for sale.
Buy each garage as you can afford it.
The trophy pops when all 8 garage properties are owned.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles in the Scooter Bros app. Open the app on your in-game phone, add a vehicle you own or have found, and repeat for 10 different vehicles. Each vehicle counts once, so register ten distinct ones — the same vehicle twice does not help.
trophies.name: On the Spot
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app on your in-game phone.
Register a vehicle you own or have found.
Repeat for 10 different vehicles; the trophy pops on the tenth.
